_comment: Per-dataset overrides for scripts/dataset_sweep.py, keyed by filename.
Every field is optional. Omit a dataset entirely and the sweep confirms
whatever schema detection suggested -- which is worth doing deliberately,
because it exercises the same guess the user is offered at the checkpoint.
'note' is the point of each entry: it says which dataset *shape* the file
is standing in for, so a sweep's table reads as coverage rather than as a
list of filenames. The shapes still uncovered are listed at the bottom.
'in_repo': false marks a dataset that lives only on the machine running
the sweep. Only data/examples/*.csv is committed -- the bigger and messier
shapes are exactly the ones too large to version -- so those entries are
exempt from the test that checks every named file actually exists.

datasets.note: baseline: small, mixed numeric + categorical, binary target, PII columns present
regression route: KFold, no resampling, r2/RMSE, plus a date column and an ordinal (epc_rating)
imbalanced + 50k rows: the SMOTE-inside-the-fold path, and the first size at which EDA cost is visible
datasets._in_repo_note: Too large to commit; regenerate with data/_make_fraud.py.
datasets._time_column_note: Sent only on a build with time-ordered CV (PR #26). Until that merges the API rejects the field and the sweep records a confirm failure -- which is the honest outcome, not a random split reported as ordered.

_shapes_not_yet_covered: wide: 100+ columns -- the report agent's prompt budget, flagged untested in BUILD_PLAN section 9
multiclass: >2 classes, for the OvR ROC-AUC branch and the absent PR-AUC
numeric-only: forces K-Means rather than K-Prototypes
high-cardinality text / free-text columns: the FrequencyEncoder and 'text' role
small n: a few hundred rows, against the fold and cluster minimums
messy: mixed dtypes in one column, an all-null column, duplicate headers, unicode names
